references.text: The parallel account in Matthew also tells of Joseph of Arimathea, a rich man who was a disciple of Jesus ([ref:Matt 27:57|Matthew 27:57]).
Mark's parallel account describes Joseph of Arimathea as a highly respected member of the Council, who was also waiting for God's kingdom ([ref:Mark 15:43|Mark 15:43]).
John's account mentions Joseph of Arimathea as a secret disciple of Jesus, out of fear of the Jews ([ref:Joh 19:38|John 19:38]).
Simeon is described in a similar way as a "righteous and devout" man, a parallel to the description of Joseph as "good and righteous" ([ref:Luk 2:25|Luke 2:25]).
The next verse clarifies that Joseph had not agreed with the Council's decision and action, and that he was from Arimathea and waiting for God's kingdom ([ref:Luk 23:51|Luke 23:51]).
Isaiah's prophecy that the Lord's suffering servant would be buried with a rich man is fulfilled through the wealthy council member Joseph providing Jesus' burial ([ref:Jes 53:9|Isaiah 53:9]).
Proverbs says that a good person finds favor with the Lord – Joseph is described precisely as a "good and righteous" man ([ref:Ordsp 12:2|Proverbs 12:2]).
The Council (Sanhedrin) had demanded Jesus' death, but Joseph stood out as a righteous man among them ([ref:Luk 23:13-25|Luke 23:13-25]).
